title: How much work disappears with one process?
description: Choose an executor shape and failure event, then change cluster width and task duration. The model shows useful parallelism, memory per concurrent task, invalidated shuffle output, and recovery waves.

shapes.label: Compact executors
shapes.detail: 4 cores, 18 GiB heap, and 3 GiB overhead. More processes reduce the work lost with one executor.

shapes.label: Balanced executors
shapes.detail: 8 cores, 32 GiB heap, and 5 GiB overhead. A moderate process boundary for mixed stages.

shapes.label: Dense executors
shapes.detail: 16 cores, 56 GiB heap, and 8 GiB overhead. Fewer processes save overhead but share memory and fate across more slots.

failures.label: No failure
failures.detail: Establish the healthy stage duration and memory envelope.

failures.label: Lose one executor
failures.detail: One process, its active tasks, cached blocks, and local shuffle output disappear.

failures.label: Interrupt 25% of executors
failures.detail: A node-pool or spot interruption removes a correlated set of executor processes.

notice: The model assumes 60% of executor heap is available to concurrent execution work and evenly distributed shuffle and cache blocks. Production sizing must use measured row width, spill, garbage collection, Python or native memory, decommissioning, external shuffle storage, and platform replacement time.
